title: 第一章 鬼画符
content_zh:
江砚这辈子，最烦的就是写字。

    从小学起，他的作业本就没干净过。老师拿红笔在他卷子上批过一句话，他到现在还记得：“字如其人，你这字，心是野的。”那时候他不服气——字写得快怎么了？同样一道题，别人一笔一画描半天，他唰唰几下就完事，省下的工夫够打两局游戏。

    到了大学，这毛病更没人管了。期末赶论文，三千字的检讨他能写出五千字的潦草，连他自己回头都认不全。同寝室的哥们儿管他那手字叫“鬼画符”，说他写一个“龙”字，能让人看出三条蛇打架。江砚也不恼，咧嘴一乐：“能认就行，又不是写给裱画的。”

    这天晚上，雨下得邪乎。

    不是那种淅淅沥沥的雨，是瓢泼，一阵一阵地砸在宿舍楼的铁皮雨棚上，咚咚咚，像有人在头顶上擂鼓。整栋楼的人都睡了，就他一个，台灯底下趴着，对着一沓白纸发愁。

    白天他翘了三节课，被辅导员逮了个正着，勒令写一篇“深刻的”检讨，不少于两千字，明早交。江砚捏着笔，憋了半宿，才憋出个开头。他写检讨从来都是糊弄，可今晚不知怎的，笔下格外不听话。墨水仿佛是活的，顺着笔尖往外淌，他越写越快，越写越乱，到后来，那些字几乎连成了一片，一笔不停，密密麻麻爬满了整整一页。

    他自己都看愣了。

    这页纸上的字，他一个都认不出来。不是潦草那种认不出，是——那根本不像字。横不是横，竖不是竖，弯弯绕绕勾连在一处，像谁拿墨在纸上撒了一把活蚯蚓。可偏偏，盯久了，那一团乱麻里又透出某种说不清的章法，像水里的漩涡，把人的眼睛往里吸。

    江砚揉了揉眼。一定是熬太晚了。

    窗外一道闪电劈下来，惨白的光透进屋，照得满桌的纸刺眼。紧跟着是炸雷，震得玻璃嗡嗡响。台灯“啪”地灭了，整间屋子陷进黑里。

    “……跳闸了？”江砚嘟囔一声，伸手去摸手机。

    可他的手没摸到手机。

    他的指尖触到的，是一片冰凉的、湿漉漉的东西，黏腻地缠上来，顺着手腕往上爬。那不是水，更像是某种有温度——或者说，有意志的东西。江砚一个激灵想缩手，却发现自己整条胳膊都动不了了，像是陷进了一摊化不开的浓墨里。

    黑暗里，他听见一个声音。

    那声音不是从耳朵进来的，是直接在脑子里响的，又轻又远，像隔着千百年的风：

    “……心手相通者……可执此笔……”

    江砚想问“谁”，可他张不开嘴。那片黑暗张开了，像一张没有底的口，把他连人带魂，整个吞了进去。下坠的感觉没完没了，四面八方都是那行他认不出的“鬼画符”，密密麻麻地围着他转，越转越快，最后拧成一个点，扎进他眉心。

    他眼前最后闪过的，是桌上那页写满了怪字的纸。
content_en:
The most annoying thing in Jiang Yan's life is writing.

    His homework has never been clean since elementary school. The teacher used a red pen to mark a sentence on his paper. He still remembers it to this day: "The words are just like the person, and you have a wild heart." At that time, he was not convinced - what happened to the writing speed? For the same question, it would take a long time for others to paint it one stroke at a time, but he could finish it in just a few strokes, saving enough time to play two games.

    When I got to college, no one cared about this problem anymore. When he was rushing to write a paper at the end of the term, he could scribble out a 3,000-word review of 5,000 words, and he couldn't even read it when he looked back. The buddies in my dormitory called his calligraphy "ghost-drawing talisman" and said that when he wrote the character "dragon", people could see three snakes fighting. Jiang Yan was not annoyed and grinned happily: "As long as you can recognize it, it's not written for mounting."

    That night, it rained terribly.

    It wasn't the kind of drizzle, it was pouring, hitting the iron awning of the dormitory building one after another, like someone beating a drum above their heads. Everyone in the whole building was asleep, but he was the only one, lying under the lamp, worrying about a pile of white paper.

    During the day, he skipped three classes and was caught by the counselor. He was ordered to write a "profound" self-reflection of no less than 2,000 words and was due tomorrow morning. Jiang Yan held the pen in his hand and held it in for half a night before he finally came up with the beginning. He was always fooling around when writing reviews, but tonight for some reason, his writing was particularly disobedient. The ink seemed to be alive, flowing out from the tip of the pen. He wrote faster and faster, and the more he wrote, the more chaotic he became. Eventually, the words were almost connected into one piece, and they filled the entire page with one stroke without stopping.

    He himself was stunned.

    He couldn't recognize any of the words on the page. It’s not that it’s so scrawled that it’s unrecognizable, it’s that it doesn’t look like writing at all. The horizontal lines are not horizontal, and the vertical lines are not vertical. They are connected in one place, like someone took ink and sprinkled a handful of live earthworms on the paper. But unfortunately, after staring for a long time, there is some indescribable structure revealed in the mess, like a whirlpool in the water, sucking people's eyes in.

    Jiang Yan rubbed his eyes. Must have stayed up too late.

    A bolt of lightning struck outside the window, and pale light penetrated into the room, illuminating the paper on the table. Then came the thunder, which made the glass buzz. The desk lamp went out with a bang, and the whole room was plunged into darkness.

    "...The circuit breaker tripped?" Jiang Yan muttered and reached out to touch his phone.

    But his hand didn't touch the phone.

    What his fingertips touched was a piece of cold, wet stuff, sticky and sticky, crawling up his wrist. It's not water, it's more like something with temperature - or, in other words, will. Jiang Yan was agitated and wanted to shrink his hand, but found that his entire arm could not move, as if he was stuck in a pool of thick ink that could not be dissolved.

    In the darkness, he heard a voice.

    The voice didn't come from the ears, it rang directly in my head. It was light and far away, as if separated by thousands of years of wind:

    "...Those who have the same mind and hand...can hold this pen..."

    Jiang Yan wanted to ask "who", but he couldn't open his mouth. The darkness opened up, like a bottomless mouth, swallowing him whole including his soul. The falling feeling was endless, and there were lines of "ghost-drawing symbols" that he could not recognize in all directions, densely surrounding him, spinning faster and faster, and finally twisted into a point and pierced the center of his eyebrows.

    The last thing that flashed before his eyes was the page on the table filled with strange words.
